introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : `points` de l'exercice = somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc ; pour la question 7, 8 et 9 de la Section II, c'est le total d'un seul jeu de sous-parties (a+b+c = d+e+f = 20), les deux jeux étant au choix.
Scan avec fantômes du verso (texte miroir qui transparaît) : relu en image sur la page nettoyée, aucun mot illisible dans les énoncés retenus.
Question 9 : jeux (a, b, c) ou (d, e, f) au choix. 9(b) : « Magnesuim-28 » est une coquille du sujet (Magnesium-28), corrigée dans l'énoncé ; le sujet note la demi-vie 21 jours.

9(b)(iii) : équation donnée pour deux émissions bêta successives, 28Mg -> 28Si + 2 bêta- (les antineutrinos sont omis, niveau O Level) ; en réalité le Mg-28 passe par l'aluminium 28 (demi-vie 2,2 min) avant le silicium 28.

9(c)(i) : les traces des particules alpha et bêta à tracer par l'élève sont décrites dans le corrigé. 9(c)(ii) : le sujet ne dit pas lesquelles des propriétés sont attendues ; retenues : grande masse, fort pouvoir ionisant, faible pouvoir de pénétration (portée courte).

9(f), figure (nommée « Figure 5 » dans le sujet, déjà utilisée en 8(e)) : la flèche sur le conducteur pointe vers A (sens du courant de B vers A) ; le pôle N est à gauche et le pôle S à droite, donc le champ va de la gauche vers la droite. Par la règle de la main gauche de Fleming, la force est perpendiculaire au plan de la feuille, dirigée vers l'intérieur de la page (en s'éloignant du lecteur). Le sujet écrit « the force on the coil » en (ii) alors qu'il s'agit du conducteur AB : lu comme la force sur le conducteur.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define a semiconductor. *[2 marks]*

Differentiate between:

(ii) Intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors. *[2 marks]*

(iii) P-type and n-type semiconductors. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A **semiconductor** is a material whose **electrical conductivity lies between that of a conductor and that of an insulator**, and which conducts better as its temperature rises or when impurities are added. Examples: silicon and germanium.

**(ii)**

| Intrinsic semiconductor | Extrinsic semiconductor |
|---|---|
| A **pure** semiconductor with no impurity added (pure silicon or germanium). | A semiconductor to which a small amount of **impurity has been added (doped)**. |
| Free electrons and holes are produced in **equal numbers** by heat; very poor conductor at room temperature. | Has many more charge carriers of one kind; **much better conductivity**. |

**(iii)**

| p-type | n-type |
|---|---|
| Doped with a **trivalent** impurity (3 valence electrons: boron, aluminium, gallium), called an acceptor. | Doped with a **pentavalent** impurity (5 valence electrons: phosphorus, arsenic, antimony), called a donor. |
| **Holes** are the majority charge carriers (electrons are the minority). | **Free electrons** are the majority charge carriers (holes are the minority). |

questions.enonce_markdown:
Magnesium-28, $^{28}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$, is unstable and has a half-life of 21 days. It is known to emit beta particles.

(i) Name the particles that constitute the nucleus of an atom. *[2 marks]*

(ii) How many neutrons are in $^{28}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$? *[2 marks]*

(iii) If $^{28}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$ nucleus emits two beta particles, write a balanced decay equation. *[2 marks]*

(iv) If initially there are 200 radioactive atoms of $^{28}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$, how many radioactive atoms will be left after 42 days? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The nucleus is made of **protons** (positively charged) and **neutrons** (no charge), together called **nucleons**.

**(ii)** Number of neutrons $N = A - Z = 28 - 12 = \mathbf{16}$ neutrons.

**(iii)** Each beta-minus emission turns a neutron into a proton, so the atomic number rises by 1 each time and the mass number does not change. After two emissions $Z = 12 + 2 = 14$, which is silicon:

$$^{28}_{12}\mathrm{Mg} \rightarrow {}^{28}_{14}\mathrm{Si} + 2\,{}^{\;0}_{-1}\mathrm{e}$$

Check: mass number $28 = 28 + 0$; charge (atomic number) $12 = 14 + 2 \times (-1)$.

**(iv)** $42\,\mathrm{days} = 2 \times 21\,\mathrm{days}$, that is **2 half-lives**. The number of undecayed atoms is halved each half-life:

$$200 \rightarrow 100 \rightarrow 50$$

**$50$ radioactive atoms of $^{28}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$ will be left** (equivalently $200 \times (\tfrac{1}{2})^{2} = 50$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Sketch the tracks of alpha and beta particles in cloud chambers. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Name the three properties responsible for the shape of the alpha tracks. *[3 marks]*

(iii) State one use of radioactivity. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Sketches to draw (two small drawings, labelled):

- **Alpha track:** a **short, thick, straight** line, starting at the source and ending abruptly (about $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ in air).
- **Beta track:** a **longer, thin, thread-like line**, **not straight** (it may be curved or wavy and change direction), because the light beta particles are easily deflected.

**(ii)** The alpha tracks are straight, thick and short because alpha particles have:

1. a **large mass** (heavy particles are not deflected when they collide with air molecules), so the track is **straight**;
2. a **strong ionising power** (charge $+2$ and large size), so they leave many droplets along the path and the track is **thick**;
3. a **low penetrating power**, they lose their energy quickly and stop after a few centimetres of air, so the track is **short**.

**(iii)** Any one of: **sterilising** medical instruments and food with gamma rays; **treating cancer** (radiotherapy); **radioactive dating** of fossils and rocks (carbon-14); **tracers** in medicine and industry; **checking the thickness** of paper and metal sheets; smoke detectors.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define an electromagnet. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Name a material which is suitable for the core of an electromagnet and state the property which makes it suitable. *[2 marks]*

(iii) State two ways by which the strength of an electromagnet can be increased. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** An **electromagnet** is a **temporary magnet** made by passing an electric current through a coil of insulated wire (usually wound on a soft iron core); it is magnetic only while the current flows.

**(ii)** The core is made of **soft iron**. It is suitable because it is **easily magnetised and easily demagnetised** (it loses its magnetism as soon as the current is switched off).

**(iii)** Any two of: **increase the current** in the coil; **increase the number of turns** of the coil; use a **soft iron core** (or a bigger core); make the coil shorter so the turns are closer together.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transformer is constructed with a primary coil of 400 turns and a secondary coil of 200 turns.

(i) Name the two types of transformers. *[2 marks]*

(ii) If the primary coil is connected to a $240\,\mathrm{V}$ a.c mains, determine the secondary voltage. *[3 marks]*

(iii) Name one cause of energy losses in practical transformers. *[1 mark]*

(iv) State what can be done to minimize the above named cause of energy loss. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** The **step-up transformer** (more turns on the secondary than on the primary, so it raises the voltage) and the **step-down transformer** (fewer turns on the secondary, so it lowers the voltage).

**(ii)** For an ideal transformer:

$$\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \quad\Rightarrow\quad V_s = V_p \times \frac{N_s}{N_p} = 240 \times \frac{200}{400} = 120\,\mathrm{V}$$

**The secondary voltage is $120\,\mathrm{V}$** (this is a step-down transformer).

**(iii)** One cause of energy loss: **eddy currents** induced in the iron core, which heat the core. (Other causes: resistance of the copper windings, hysteresis in the core, leakage of magnetic flux.)

**(iv)** Make the core from **thin laminated sheets of soft iron**, insulated from each other, so that the eddy currents are small. (To reduce the heating in the windings, use **thick copper wire** of low resistance.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 5 shows a current-carrying conductor, AB, lying in a magnetic field.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_9_fig_1.png)

*Figure 5*

(i) State the law which is used to determine the direction of the force on the conductor. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State any three ways by which the force on the coil can be increased. *[3 marks]*

(iii) State the direction in which the conductor AB will move. *[1 mark]*

(iv) State one device whose functioning depends on the application of the set up in figure 5. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **Fleming's left-hand rule** (motor rule): hold the thumb, the first finger and the second finger of the left hand at right angles to each other. If the **First** finger points along the **F**ield (from N to S) and the **seCond** finger along the **C**urrent (conventional current direction), then the **thuMb** points in the direction of the force, that is the **M**otion of the conductor.

**(ii)** Any three of: **increase the current** in the conductor; use a **stronger magnet** (increase the magnetic field strength); **increase the length of the conductor** in the field (for a coil, increase the number of turns); place the conductor **at right angles** to the field (the force is greatest then).

**(iii)** The magnetic field goes from the N pole (left) to the S pole (right), that is, **to the right**, and the current flows from B to A, that is, **upwards** in the figure. By Fleming's left-hand rule the force is at right angles to both, so the conductor AB moves **perpendicular to the plane of the paper, into the page** (away from the reader).

**(iv)** Any one of: the **electric motor**; the moving-coil loudspeaker; the moving-coil ammeter or galvanometer.
